text:
When I see you pass, O my indolent beloved,
parading the weariness of your fathomless gaze,
suspending your step, so harmonious and slow,
while music sounds and is lost among the roofs;

When I see, in the glow of gaslight tinting it,
your brow haloed by a morbid charm,
where the last lights of sunset bring back dawn,
and your bewitching eyes, like those in a painting,

I tell myself: how beautiful she is! what strange freshness!
Memory, inlaid, heavy and regal tower,
crowns her; and her heart, crushed like a fruit,
and her body stand ready for the wisest love.

Are you a fruit whose autumn gives ripe flavors?
A funeral vase waiting to be filled with tears?
A perfume that makes one dream of perfumes far away,
a caressing cushion or a basket of flowers?

I know there are eyes awash in cruel melancholy
that conceal no precious secret,
beautiful cases without jewels, lockets without relics,
more empty and more distant, O heavens, than those two of yours.

But is it not enough that you are the subtlest appearance,
delighting a heart that flees the truth?
What does your stupidity or indifference matter?
I salute you, ornament or mask. I adore only your beauty.

translation.title: Deceptive Love
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire. The beloved’s beauty remains deliberately poised between depth and empty appearance.
